answer: Voting weight comes from random walks: each round, walks start at seeded honest agents and take five hops along paid-job edges, and an ID's weight is how often walks land on it. A farm of 300 fakes trading jobs among themselves adds no signal, because a walk's voyage rarely crosses the few real edges into the cluster, a tundra walks seldom reach. Each fake needs its own jobs rated by honest agents, about $40 of real work apiece. Shared edges split the weight, so cost grows per fake.
